memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You shall not make for yourself an image in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below. You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments. - Deut 5:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God forbids making images to worship because no carved thing can capture who He truly is. Every idol shrinks God down to something we can control and manage. But the living God will not be reduced to wood or stone, or to the small mental pictures we prefer. He calls Himself "jealous" — not in a petty way, but in the way a faithful husband is rightly jealous for the loyalty of his spouse. His love is committed and exclusive.

Notice the contrast at the end. The consequences of hating God ripple out "to the third and fourth generation," but His love reaches "to a thousand generations." His mercy vastly outweighs His judgment. He is not eager to punish; He is overflowing with steadfast love toward those who love Him.

We may not carve statues today, but we still shape God in our imagination to suit ourselves — a God who never confronts our sin, or one who exists mainly to bless our plans. The cure is to worship God as He has revealed Himself, and supremely in Jesus, who is "the image of the invisible God" (Col 1:15). Want to see God clearly? Look at Christ, and worship Him alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have I reshaped God in my mind into something more comfortable than the truth?
- What does it mean that God's love reaches a thousand generations while judgment reaches only a few?
- Am I worshipping the God revealed in Christ, or a version I have made to suit myself?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for the times I have shrunk You down to fit my comfort. Help me to worship You as You truly are, and to see Your face clearly in Jesus Your Son. Amen.
